explanation.text: The Logic: AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) is the industry association of SEBI-registered Asset Management Companies. It is not a regulator and not a Self-Regulatory Organization; SEBI is the regulator of mutual funds in India. The Trap: AMFI is sometimes mistaken for a regulator or an SRO, but the workbook explicitly notes it is neither. Its role is industry promotion, distributor registration, and code-of-conduct administration. Note: Mutual fund distributors register with AMFI to obtain their ARN, and the AMFI Code of Conduct for Intermediaries sets ethical standards that distributors must follow.
